title: Preparation of Cells for Transmission Electron Microscopy Ultrastructural Analysis
author: Jillian C Danne
materials: To check the region of interest:

steps.title: Prepare Cells for Fixation
steps.instruction: Prepare cells based on their growth state, ensuring all steps are performed in a fume hood with appropriate PPE.

substeps.instruction: For suspended cells in 1.5 ml microcentrifuge or 15 ml Falcon® tubes: centrifuge at 1200 rpm for 2 minutes, remove supernatant, and gently resuspend cell pellets in solution using a pipette.
For adherent cells: remove cell culture media from the well-plate or petri dish.

steps.title: Primary Fixation
steps.instruction: Fix cells using Karnovsky's fixative (2% PFA, 2.5% glutaraldehyde in 0.1M cacodylate buffer, pH 7.2).

substeps.instruction: Adherent cells: Add fixative to the well-plate or petri dish, seal the lid with parafilm, and fix for 2 hours at room temperature or overnight at 4°C with agitation.
Suspended cells: Resuspend the cell pellet in 1 ml of fixative and fix for 2 hours at room temperature or overnight at 4°C with agitation.

steps.title: Wash Cells
steps.instruction: Remove fixative and wash cells with 0.1M cacodylate buffer (3 x 10 minutes) at room temperature with agitation.

steps.title: Post-Fixation
steps.instruction: Post-fix cells in 1% Osmium tetroxide and 1.5% potassium ferrocyanide in 0.1M cacodylate buffer for 1 hour at room temperature with agitation, ensuring lids are well-secured.

substeps.instruction: Handle osmium tetroxide in a fume hood with PPE; discard used osmium in a labeled plastic container containing ethanol.

steps.title: Final Wash and Storage
steps.instruction: Wash samples in MilliQ water (3 x 10 minutes) at room temperature with agitation. Samples may be stored at 4°C for up to 1 week.

substeps.instruction: If handling suspended cells, proceed to the agarose embedding steps (Step 6 onwards).

steps.title: Prepare Agarose Embedding
steps.instruction: Prepare and apply 4% aqueous ultra-pure agarose to suspended cell pellets.

substeps.instruction: Melt 4% aqueous ultra-pure agarose using a Bain Marie water bath (boiling water) or a heat block set to 95°C.
Remove supernatant and add approximately 100 μl (2 drops) of pre-warmed agarose to the cell pellet.
Gently vortex to homogeneously resuspend the pellet in agarose.
Optional: To concentrate the pellet, return the tube to the Bain Marie/heat block until liquefied, then pellet cells using a benchtop microcentrifuge.

steps.title: Solidify and Section Agarose Block
steps.instruction: Solidify the agarose and cut into small cubes for processing.

substeps.instruction: Cool the agarose-cell mixture at 4°C for 10 minutes to solidify.
Cut the extreme tip of the microcentrifuge tube with a razor blade and push the sample out using a wooden stick.
Place the block on a Teflon plate or dental wax sheet; cut the block in half with a scalpel or double-edged razor blade.
Cut halves into strips, then into cubes no larger than 1mm³.
Transfer cubes into a 5ml tube using forceps.

steps.title: Ethanol Dehydration Series
steps.instruction: Dehydrate samples through an increasing ethanol gradient. Each step is performed for 1 hour at room temperature with agitation. If using a PELCO BioWave® Pro+ Microwave Processing System, use settings: 40 seconds, 150W, No vacuum.

substeps.instruction: 30% ethanol in MilliQ water
50% ethanol in MilliQ water
70% ethanol in MilliQ water (can be left at 4°C overnight if necessary)
90% ethanol in MilliQ water
95% ethanol in MilliQ water
100% ethanol
100% anhydrous ethanol (Type 3Å molecular sieves may be added to stock solution)

steps.title: Acetone Dehydration
steps.instruction: Dehydrate samples in acetone. Each step is performed for 1 hour at room temperature with agitation. If using BioWave, use settings: 40 seconds, 150W, No vacuum.

substeps.instruction: 100% acetone (Propylene oxide can be used as an alternative)
100% anhydrous acetone (Type 3Å molecular sieves may be added to stock solution)

steps.title: Epon Resin Infiltration
steps.instruction: Infiltrate samples with Epon resin. Use BioWave settings: 3 minutes, 250W, Vacuum on. Ensure samples sink in solution; if they float, extend infiltration times.

substeps.instruction: Optional: 100% anhydrous acetone : epon resin (3:1 ratio) overnight at room temperature with agitation.
100% anhydrous acetone : epon resin (1:1 ratio) for 6 hours at room temperature with agitation.
100% anhydrous acetone : epon resin (1:3 ratio) overnight at room temperature with agitation.
100% epon resin for 6 hours at room temperature with agitation.
100% epon resin overnight at room temperature with agitation (a third 100% resin step may be required if residual acetone is present).

steps.title: Polymerization
steps.instruction: Transfer samples to labeled plastic embedding moulds, flat bottom BEEM® capsules, or standard tip BEEM® capsules containing 100% epon resin. Polymerize in an oven at 60°C for 24-48 hours.

steps.title: Block Trimming
steps.instruction: Trim the resin-embedded block to expose the cells.

substeps.instruction: Mount the block in an ultramicrotome chuck and secure to a stereo microscope mount.
Manually trim the front face and four edges into a trapezoid shape using a double-edge razor blade.

Transfer to a Leica UC7 ultramicrotome; trim the front surface using a 0.5 μm feed and a 45° glass knife (6.4 mm or 8 mm thickness) or a Diatome 35° ultra semi diamond knife until a full face of cells is obtained.

steps.title: Ultrathin Sectioning
steps.instruction: Cut 90 nm gold-colored ultrathin sections at 1 mm/sec using a Leica UC7 ultramicrotome and a Diatome 45° ultra wet diamond knife.

substeps.instruction: Spread sections using a Max Wax heat pen to prevent wrinkles.
Pick up sections on 50-200 mesh copper or palladium-coated copper grids.
Place grids section side up on filter paper, cover with a glass petri dish, and dry for 10 minutes.
Store grids in an enclosed grid box.

steps.title: Semi-Thin Sectioning and Screening
steps.instruction: Cut 500 nm semi-thin sections at 1 mm/sec using a Leica UC7 ultramicrotome and 45° glass knife (with filtered water-filled boat) or suitable diamond knife.

substeps.instruction: Retrieve sections with an eyelash or Dalmatian hair on a wooden stick; float in a drop of MilliQ water on a slide, then dry on a mini hot plate.
Stain with Toluidine blue solution for 10-20 seconds on a mini hot plate, rinse with MilliQ water, and dry on a mini hot plate.
Observe with a wide-field light microscope; if the region of interest is not found, trim deeper and repeat.

steps.title: Post-Sectioning Staining
steps.instruction: Stain grids using a parafilm-covered flat bench/glass board with water underneath. Transfer grids section side down using fine forceps or a perfect loop. Use 100-200 μl drops for MilliQ water and 50-100 μl for stains.

substeps.instruction: Stain with 0.6% filtered uranyl acetate in MilliQ water for 3 minutes (store solution in foil in a dark place).
Rinse 5 x 1 minute in MilliQ water.
Stain with 0.1-0.4% filtered lead citrate in MilliQ water for 3 minutes (add 4 drops of 10M sodium hydroxide to stock solution prior to use).
Rinse 5 x 1 minute in MilliQ water.

steps.title: Final Drying and Imaging
steps.instruction: Place grids section side up on filter paper, cover with a glass petri dish, and dry for 10 minutes. Store in a grid storage box.

substeps.instruction: Place grid in a TEM holder for high-resolution imaging (e.g., JEOL JEM-1400-Plus TEM at 80 keV with CMOS 'Flash' camera).

steps.title: Alternative Adherent Cell Recovery
steps.instruction: If required, recover adherent cells for processing.

substeps.instruction: Gently detach adherent cells from the well-plate/petri dish using a cell scraper.
Transfer cells to a 1.5 ml microcentrifuge tube using a 3 ml or 1000 μl transfer pipette and pellet at 1200 rpm for 2 minutes.
